# About Lena

- Supervises a claims team at a carrier focused on trucking, still fairly new to commercial lines
- Came to claims from writing estimates at a collision shop (Brightway Collision)
- Family on her father's side is Nigerian; Okafor is an Igbo name

# Dashcams and Evidence in Trucking

- Dashcam video is far more common in trucking than in most lines
  - Nearly every insured fleet has drivers run a cab dashcam
  - Claims cannot log into the fleet's camera system; the insured has to send each clip
  - Rear impacts stay hard to call because the camera faces forward
- Lost or recorded-over footage has not come up for her in trucking, though she has never tracked it
  - Fleets keep their own video for their safety programs
  - The carrier sets no retention rule; storage is up to the fleet
- Telematics is offered but sits with loss control or service, not claims
- Warehouse or third-party camera footage is requested only when the file lacks evidence
- Without video: driver statements, scene photos, phone clips, the police report, repair estimates
  - Damage patterns often decide it; pure word against word is decided as such
  - A late police report can reopen a liability decision

# Payments, Coverage and Ideas

- Long payment delays are uncommon and depend on the claim
  - Most come from open coverage questions (effective dates, added units, excluded cargo)
  - Also from waiting on busy fleet owners for driver lists, bills of lading and records
  - Insureds are told at first notice to keep damage from getting worse; rental and downtime coverage exist
- No AI on the claims side for checking a policy against evidence
- Pitch Day idea: a tool that drafts the customer follow-up email after each adjuster call
  - Not prompted by a service problem; about consistency as the commercial book grows
- Ideas go to her manager and up the chain; she suggests but does not decide purchases
- Adjusters see more day-to-day detail than a supervisor
  - Offered to ask an adjuster to talk with Alex and pass along a profile link

# To Do

- **Check back with Lena on the adjuster introduction**
